issue.title: Accept statements separated by semicolons
issue.body:
Our bank in Zurich exports CSV with semicolons between the columns, which is
also what Excel uses with Swiss settings. Amounts use a dot for decimals, and I
renamed the header to `date;amount;description`, but the upload is rejected at
row 1 with 'Malformed row: the number of columns does not match the header'.
Replacing every semicolon with a comma makes the file import, but that breaks
descriptions that contain commas. Could the upload accept semicolon-separated
files too?
## Discussion

### lena-k (maintainer) · 2026-11-06
Do your bank's files ever mix the two, or is it always semicolons?

### zurich-treasury-ab · 2026-11-06
Always semicolons, for both our accounts there. A description is in double
quotes when it contains a semicolon.

input.title: Accept semicolon-separated statements in the CSV parser
input.body:
File: src/ingest/parser.ts

Detect the delimiter from the header line (semicolon if it has more semicolons than commas outside quotes, otherwise comma) and pass it to splitFields, which currently hardcodes ",". The header is also split with a plain split(","), so it should use the same delimiter-aware splitting. Quoted fields keep working as before, so descriptions containing semicolons in double quotes parse correctly. Comma-separated files behave unchanged.

file: src/ingest/parser.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The parser only splits on commas: splitFields hardcodes "," and the header is read with split(","). A semicolon-separated header therefore becomes one column, and every row fails with errors.rowShape. parseStatement is called from `previewStatement` before the file is stored, which is why the upload is rejected straight away. Supporting semicolons means detecting the delimiter from the header line and using it for the header and the rows. I've opened a draft PR (pr-5) that proposes this change.
